answer: In an agent marketplace serving a glacier research station, a farm on a knoll, and a coastal haven, each identity must lock 100 tokens for 30 days to cast one vote on shared spending. Creating accounts is cheap, but activating 1,000 fake voters requires locking 100,000 tokens for the full month. The bond makes voting power depend on committed capital, so an attacker must finance every extra vote and forgo other uses of those funds.
